explanation: Rubik, who taught design in Budapest, built it to help students think about moving shapes in three dimensions. It took him about a month to solve his own puzzle.

claims.text: Ernő Rubik invented the Rubik's Cube in Hungary in 1974.
The Rubik's Cube was not invented in Japan, Poland or Austria.
Rubik taught design in Budapest and made the cube to help students think about movement in three dimensions.
It took Rubik about a month to solve his cube for the first time.

evidence.restatement: Rubik taught interior design at the Academy of Applied Arts and Crafts in Budapest. That he made the cube as a teaching aid for thinking about three-dimensional movement is widely repeated, but other accounts say his aim was the structural problem of a block whose parts turn without the whole falling apart.

claimResults.note: Checker doubt: accounts of his purpose disagree, and no search was possible in this run to settle it.

evidence.restatement: Rubik is often said to have needed about a month to solve his own cube the first time, but accounts vary, and I cannot pin the figure.

claimResults.note: Checker doubt on the figure; needs a source or a bounded wording.

issues.note: Checker doubt on c3: that Rubik built the cube to help students think about movement in three dimensions is widely repeated but contested; other accounts give the structural problem of a cube whose parts move independently. Rewrite to what all sources agree on (he taught design in Budapest) or source the purpose.
Checker doubt on c4: 'about a month' to solve it for the first time could not be checked, and accounts vary. Source it or drop it.

evidence.restatement: Ernő Rubik created the Magic Cube (Rubik's Cube) in Budapest in 1974.
Rubik invented the cube in Hungary; there is no claim that it began in Japan, Poland or Austria.
Rubik taught at the Budapest College of Applied Arts and built the cube as a classroom aid for three-dimensional movement.
Rubik has said it took him about a month to solve his first cube.
